$comment: Controlled vocabularies. scripts/validate.py enforces that every question uses only these values.

arc.$comment: Where the question belongs in the shape of an interview.
arc.opener: First 5 minutes. Low stakes, high specificity. Gets the guest talking in concrete detail before they can retreat into talking points.
arc.warmup: Minutes 5-15. Establishes the world and its vocabulary for the audience. Still safe for the guest.
arc.core: The body of the episode. Substantive but not confrontational. Most questions live here.
arc.deep: Requires earned trust. Ask after the guest has relaxed and after you have demonstrated you understand their world.
arc.pivot: Redirects a stalled or evasive stretch. Use out of order, on demand.
arc.closer: Last 10 minutes. Wide aperture, forward-looking, or reflective. Gives the guest a good last taste.

depth.light: Answerable in a sentence or two. Low risk of an evasive answer.
depth.medium: Needs a story or a worked example. The guest has to think.
depth.probing: Touches ego, money, blame, or professional consensus. Can go wrong. Ask deliberately.

theme.origin: How they got here, the path in, the accident or intention of it.
theme.craft: The actual work. Skill, tools, taste, tacit knowledge, what mastery looks like from inside.
theme.judgment: Decision-making under uncertainty, tradeoffs, the calls that don't have a right answer.
theme.failure: Mistakes, near-misses, repair, and what the field does with its errors.
theme.people: Teams, hierarchy, mentorship, clients, status, who holds power and how.
theme.money: Compensation, incentives, business model, who pays and what that distorts.
theme.change: How the field is shifting - technology, regulation, demographics, expectations.
theme.ethics: The lines, the gray zones, the pressure to cross them.
theme.myths: What outsiders get wrong, what the field misrepresents about itself.
theme.invisible: The unglamorous, unrecorded, or unpaid labor the job actually consists of.
theme.future: Where it goes next, what the guest would change, advice and legacy.
theme.personal: Cost, identity, sustainability, the life around the work.

roles.$comment: A second scoping axis, orthogonal to industry. A question can be for a role in any field - a middle manager in a hospital and in a warehouse face the same structure. Questions with no roles listed are role-agnostic and work on anyone.
roles.middle-manager: The person responsible for delivery, holding a team below and executives above. Has authority over the work but rarely over the constraints.
roles.ai-leader: Whoever owns AI strategy, adoption or enablement - director, head of AI, transformation lead. Adjacent authority rather than a manager in the middle, and often the source of the pressure managers feel.
roles.individual-contributor: A senior practitioner with no direct reports who now directs agents. Increasingly doing a version of management without the title, the training, or the authority that comes with it.
roles.builder: Whoever invented, founded or ships the tool. Unlike every other role here they have a commercial stake in the conversation and have told their origin story hundreds of times, so questions aimed at their product get the deck and questions aimed at what they have watched users actually do get something nobody else can give you.

settings.$comment: A third scoping axis: the setting the guest works in. Orthogonal to both industry and role - a middle manager at a 40,000-person insurer and a founder with six people face the same subject through completely different constraints. Questions with no settings listed work in either.
settings.enterprise: Inside a large organization. Tools arrive through procurement, IT owns the configuration, legal reviews the risk, budget runs on a cycle, and the binding constraint is usually permission rather than money or capability.
settings.entrepreneur: Running their own thing. They are procurement, IT, legal and the user at once. Nobody to ask and nobody to delegate to, the cost comes out of their own pocket, and the binding constraint is their own hours.

industries.universal: Written to land on any professional. The backbone of the database.
industries.healthcare: Clinicians, nurses, hospital administrators, public health, allied health.
industries.law: Litigators, transactional lawyers, judges, public defenders, in-house counsel.
industries.finance: Banking, investing, accounting, insurance underwriting, financial advising.
industries.technology: Software, hardware, IT, security, data, product.
industries.manufacturing: Factory operations, industrial engineering, quality, plant management.
industries.skilled-trades: Electricians, plumbers, welders, machinists, construction, HVAC.
industries.agriculture: Farming, ranching, agronomy, fisheries, food production.
industries.education: K-12 teaching, higher ed, administration, training, curriculum.
industries.hospitality: Restaurants, hotels, bars, catering, events, tourism.
industries.logistics: Freight, warehousing, supply chain, procurement, last-mile delivery.
industries.energy: Oil and gas, utilities, renewables, grid operations, nuclear.
industries.creative-arts: Musicians, writers, designers, filmmakers, visual artists, performers.
industries.nonprofit: Direct service, philanthropy, advocacy, community organizing.
industries.public-sector: Civil service, policy, regulators, municipal government, emergency services.
industries.retail-ecommerce: Store operations, merchandising, buying, DTC brands, marketplaces.
industries.real-estate: Brokerage, development, property management, appraisal, construction finance.
industries.science-research: Academic and industrial research, labs, R&D, clinical trials.
industries.sports: Athletes, coaches, trainers, scouts, front office, officials.
industries.defense-military: Active and veteran service members, defense contracting, intelligence.
